A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same study, Generalization of RLVR Using Causal Reasoning as a Testbed. All 41 pages in each version, including Appendices A–D, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2.5 fine-tuning experiments on RLCausal, CLadder deterministic-counterfactual evaluation, and reasoning-trace analyses, including the supplementary experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, with empirical outcomes reported in Figures 3–6 and Appendix D, including Tables 1–11.

M1.justification: Equation (1) revises the specified format reward from an extractability indicator to 0.5 for extractability plus 0.5 for correct answer length. This changes the documented training reward locally; the GRPO/DAPO and SFT procedures otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that training was rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same association, intervention, and counterfactual tasks over synthetic 10-variable SCMs, plus the same 790 formally represented CLadder deterministic-counterfactual problems in Appendix D.6. No dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged: GRPO, DAPO/curriculum variants, direct-answer SFT, initial models, and 7B SFT with rejection-sampled reasoning chains. Appendix B.1 newly explains the existing 'cur' labels; those comparison rows were already present in v1.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the written scoring distance by adding the missing absolute value to the total-variation formula. This revises the documented scoring rule without establishing reevaluation. Data splits, sample counts, training budgets, decoding settings, and the main 0.01 correctness threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The hint experiment, complexity analyses, reasoning-chain SFT ablation, deterministic-counterfactual test, error analyses, and extended 3B training experiment all already appear in v1. The precision plots retain their existing curves; their threshold-axis correction does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same Monte Carlo paired permutation tests with n=10000 and significance reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-estimation practice is added or revised; the existing lost-checkpoint rerun disclosure is only renumbered.

E6.justification: Figures 6 and 22–24 shift the threshold coordinates associated with the same accuracy curves by 0.01, from approximately 0–0.19 to 0.01–0.20. This corrects the reported accuracy–tolerance correspondence while retaining curve heights and rankings. All numerical entries in Tables 1–11 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 2.2 and 4.1 correct the total-variation definition by inserting absolute values. Section 3 removes the incorrect assertion that all irrelevant nodes are descendants of relevant nodes, and Figure 2 corrects the counterfactual relevant-subgraph example from 11 nodes to 10. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory findings, and conclusion retain the same central claims: RLVR generalization depends on model scale and initial reasoning competence, and successful RLVR improves marginalization strategies and reduces reasoning errors. The scope of the empirical contributions is unchanged.

C2.justification: The conclusion removes the specific conjecture that training could transfer heuristics and structured reasoning between informal and formal causal settings, replacing it with a general proposal to investigate their performance gap. The main interpretations concerning reasoning competence and counterfactual difficulty remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-and-data repository link in the abstract. Appendix A.2 clarifies that development and test sets each use 200 graphical models, and Appendix B.1 identifies the existing curriculum result labels. These improve access information and documentation without demonstrating changed datasets or runs.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. The introduction adds a citation to Zhang and Poole for variable elimination, but that work was already cited elsewhere in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized abstract and introduction edits, shortens the future-work discussion, adds acknowledgements, updates an affiliation and the publication header, and clarifies several cross-references. The section organization and overall narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes a factual-world node from relevant to irrelevant and updates its caption count. Figures 6 and 22–24 revise threshold-axis labeling, Figure 7 is reduced in size, and Figure 9 separates existing prompt bullets. These are localized display and layout revisions; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the total-variation formula and relevant-subgraph example, makes the format reward more explicit, fixes precision-plot threshold labeling, and supplies code/data access information. These provide limited gains in mathematical correctness, clarity, and reproducibility while preserving the empirical evidence and central conclusions.
